title: Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere
main_claim: The extension operator for S^2 maps L^infty(S^2) to L^p(R^3) for every p>3, i.e. the full bounded-data restriction conjecture in R^3. The route is a uniform packet-propagation bound with loss m^{10kappa+eps} for an eccentricity-biased capacity W(E)=L^{1+kappa}w^{1-kappa} (Thm pkt:main). That bound rests on a geometric propagation theorem q_* >= 1+2s-10kappa (Thm geo:main).
coverage:
Read in full and checked: Sec 0 (intro and statements); Sec 7 (global passage); Sec 5 (packets); Sec 6 (extremal argument).

Sec 7: sparse cubic lemma, including the N^2~R normalization, initial capacity K(d)<=C delta^4, the Gram/Schur joint-mass bound with the H^{-1/2} oscillatory decay and the choice of C_0, the sampling identity and lattice averaging; the L^4 constant 32 pi^3 for sigma*sigma; the peak count; the sparse covering exponents; the distributional bound and layer-cake.

Sec 5: frame identity; atomic norm and the l^3 lower bound; composition rescaling; the locality decay; the crude bounds K(c)<=m^4K(d) and gamma<=2; the refined-decoupling induction; the quartic transfer, including the scale identity r_+w_+^2 ell^4 = r_-w_-^2 and the tube-multiplicity comparison.

Sec 6: minimal time dimension s; path-count extremum, including the root-mask issue, which is handled by the #R'/#R >= m^{-o} argument; branching and pruning; incoming-degree selection; bad-vertex counting and the conditional time law; represented roots from (40) to (41); the terminal capacity arithmetic giving m^{2(1-s)+20kappa}h_1K(d), where W(F)/(f1f2)<=W(E)/(e1e2) holds; the two mass bounds and the h_1 cancellation.

Sanity checks of geo:main by hand: the bush example and the planar example. The planar one shows q_*<=3-kappa, which is consistent with the claimed 3-10kappa.

Geometric Secs 1-4 (~4,700 lines of calibrated paths, entropy profiles, projection/Furstenberg rate inequalities, three aspect cases): spot-checked only. This covered the hairbrush lemma (pair-separation and angle geometry, Cauchy-Schwarz exponent), the heavy-box count and angular-exclusion exponent arithmetic (c_kappa=4/kappa), the bounded-complexity reduction including W(AB)<=W(A)W(B), and the statement of Ren-Wang Thm 4.1 (dual Furstenberg; matches with k=t, sigma=s).

Not verified line by line: the entropy machinery of Sec 2 and the aspect-case exclusions of Sec 4, which are the decisive part. So this verdict means no gap in what was checked; it does not certify the geometric theorem.
sibling_notes: The family 077 board was empty when this audit started, so there were no sibling reports to use. The paper cites companion OpenAI papers (Kakeya maximal, Bochner-Riesz, diagonal restriction), but its main proof does not depend on them; they appear only in the consequences and remarks.
